title: Balanced and Elastic End-to-end Training of Dynamic LLMs
problem: Dynamic LLM techniques (MoE, pruning, layer freezing, sparse attention, early exit, MoD) reduce computation but introduce severe workload imbalance across workers, making them impractical for large-scale distributed training.
motivation: Need autonomous dynamic load balancing for distributed LLM training to maximize efficiency gains from dynamic computation techniques.
method: Dynamic LLM techniques like mixture-of-experts create workload imbalance—some workers do far more computation than others, slowing training as fast workers wait for slow ones. DynMo solves this by continuously measuring each worker's load and automatically reassigning tasks to balance the work. It consolidates computation onto fewer workers when efficient and operates across multiple GPUs and machine clusters.
key_novelty: DynMo guarantees the maximum possible reduction in workload imbalance while consolidating workers without slowing down training.
contributions: Autonomous dynamic load balancing algorithm with provable guarantees
Worker consolidation mechanism for releasing idle workers
Support for multi-GPU and multi-node cluster deployment
Speedup for dynamic GPT: 1.23x (MoE), 3.18x (pruning), 2.23x (layer freeze), 4.02x (sparse), 4.52x (early exit), 1.17x (MoD)
